notes: Account summary: WaveCrest builds a SaaS knowledge-base used by ~600 enterprise customers for support chat and KB search.
Primary pain: current vector search (managed DB) inconsistent at scale — recall fine but top-k quality poor; ranking costs on self-hosted reranker are high.
Scale: expects moderate index size (250k-750k unique docs, ~1.2M granular passages after chunking).
Traffic profile: high QPS on business hours — target 200-600 qps peak for embeddings+rerank pipeline; steady-state 80-150 qps.
Latency targets: 95th percentile end-to-end <200ms for retrieval+rerank; prefer <150ms for the reranker step alone. AE note: 'customer is strict on sub-200ms SLA'.
Cost sensitivity: procurement flagged per-query budget — target gross cost <$0.03 per query at projected QPS (including embedding lookups + lightweight reranker).
Architecture preference: hosted API to avoid infra ops; they'll run initial POC on Redwood hosted, later consider Dedicated if latency/cost tradeoffs require reserved capacity.

Model preferences: prefer open model family for reranker (smaller transformer reranker) and a separate embedding model with 1536-2048 dims. Open to Redwood's model recommendations; want ability to fallback to cheaper model under load.
Security: require SSO/SAML, encryption at rest with KMS, audit logs available for 180 days, and option for EU data residency for select customers.
POC acceptance criteria: ingest completeness >99%, 95p retrieval+rerank latency <=200ms under 48h peak test, MAP@10 improvement >=12% vs current baseline, cost estimate within forecasted ARR band.
Concise quotes: 'We will walk away if latency spikes above 250ms consistently' — Head of Product; 'Need a realistic cost model for 1M monthly queries' — CFO.

Suggested Redwood plays: - use Optimize recommendations for batching/quantization - enable prefix/kv caching for repeated contexts - configure routing policy to fall back to cheaper reranker variant under burst.
Procurement timeline: legal/security sign-off in parallel with POC; procurement expects decision by 2025-02 if POC satisfactory.
Open questions: exact retention windows for logs, SLA credits language, and compatibility with WaveCrest's tenant-scoped encryption keys.
